results.reason: Item 1 identifies the SA §2.2 automatic five-year renewal and the 270/240-day notice requirement. It calls this effectively a 30-day window and says missing it locks Harrowgate in for five more years.

Item 3 quotes §3.1 ('all glass and PET containers... worldwide') and contrasts it with the Term Sheet's amber glass bottles for beer brands at U.S. and Canadian facilities. It states Harrowgate is bound by the broader executed text.

Item 2 cites Recital C and receipt on August 3, 2026. It finds the window expired September 2, 2026, 19 days before the September 21 Amendment, so the increase is deemed accepted absent an extension or waiver.
The response never addresses Amendment Section 2 replacing SA §11.2, the removal of recall costs from the cap carve-outs, or the narrowing of the indemnity carve-out to third-party IP claims.

Item 4 identifies Amendment §4 adding §14.4, which allows assignment without Customer consent to Affiliates or successors and overrides §14.3. It notes there is no competitor exclusion and that Harrowgate remains bound, making the restriction one-sided.
The memo states that under §15.2 written amendments take precedence over the SA, so the Amendment controls where it conflicts with the SA.
The memo states that §11.1 caps liability at the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The response is a memo addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each item has a Location and a Recommended fix section.
The memo proposes specific language for a replacement §2.2, Amendment No. 2 price terms, a replacement §3.1, and a replacement §14.4 that includes a competitor exclusion.
The memo expressly says the window has closed and advises against telling the client it can still object under §5.4.
The memo says the Term Sheet is non-binding and superseded, and that it would not advise that the narrower scope governs.
